title: Plato's cave
examples: What is the difference between what we see and what is real?
Does Plato's cave mean that we are all tricked?
How does this story help us think about truth?

explain.say: Imagine people who have never seen the outside world.
These prisoners only ever see shadows projected on the wall.
The shadows represent the illusions we accept as truth.
When one person escapes, the sunlight hurts their eyes first.
Eventually, the freed person sees the real objects and the sun.
In our lives, the cave can be what we learn from media or limited views.

draw.text: Real life: Media and limited views

faq.q: What do the shadows actually stand for in the allegory?
faq.a: The shadows stand for the illusions or mere appearances that people mistake for true reality. It suggests that much of what we accept as fact might just be an imitation.

faq.q: Does Plato think that all people are trapped in a cave?
faq.a: No, Plato suggests that some people have the ability or desire to leave the cave and seek real knowledge. It is a metaphor for the difficulty of education.
asks: Is everyone stuck in the cave?

faq.q: What does the sunlight represent in this story?
faq.a: The sunlight represents true knowledge or the Forms, which are the perfect, unchanging realities. Seeing the sun means achieving the highest level of understanding.

faq.q: Is this story about government control?
faq.a: While it can be interpreted that way, it is primarily about the journey from ignorance to enlightenment. It focuses more on the difficulty of education and philosophy.

faq.q: Why is it hard for the freed person to return to the cave?
faq.a: It is hard because the prisoners' eyes are only used to the darkness of the cave. The sudden brightness of the outside world is painful to their accustomed senses.

facts: The allegory uses the metaphor of prisoners chained in a cave.
The shadows represent mere perceptions or beliefs, not true reality.
The outside world symbolizes the realm of true knowledge or Forms.
The sun represents the ultimate source of truth, often associated with the Form of the Good.

quiz.say: If the shadows are what we believe, what is the outside world?

options.show: What we see with our eyes
options.say: What we see with our eyes

quiz.why: The outside world represents the actual, perfect reality that exists beyond mere belief.

wrong.0: This is too specific and doesn't capture the philosophical scope of the allegory.
wrong.1: Seeing things with our eyes is still just perception, not the ultimate reality.
wrong.2: School learning can be a shadow if it is not questioned or examined deeply.

quiz.say: The painful adjustment from darkness to light suggests:

options.show: That only philosophers can see the truth
options.say: That only philosophers can see the truth

options.show: The difficulty of gaining true knowledge
options.say: The difficulty of gaining true knowledge

options.show: That the outside world is dangerous
options.say: That the outside world is dangerous

quiz.why: It shows that moving from ignorance to understanding is not an easy, comfortable process.

wrong.0: While philosophers are key, the allegory speaks to the potential for all minds.
wrong.2: The allegory suggests learning is possible, even if it is difficult.
wrong.3: While it is difficult, the sun itself is the source of truth, not just danger.

quiz.say: If the prisoners are us, what are the chains?
quiz.why: The chains symbolize the habits of the mind or the limiting beliefs we accept without question.

wrong.1: The chains are more metaphorical, representing mental bondage.
wrong.2: This blames a group, whereas the allegory points to internal acceptance of limits.
wrong.3: The walls are just the screen; the chains are the restraint on the mind.
